'''Gautam Radhakrishna Desiraju''' is an Indian [[Structural chemistry|scientist]] and an emeritus professor at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc). His research is on crystal engineering <ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Desiraju |first=Gautam R. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bfY3AQAAIAAJ |title=Crystal Engineering: The Design of Organic Solids |date=1989 |publisher=Elsevier |isbn=978-0-444-87457-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Desiraju |first1=Gautam R. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AMLWuCzDN20C |title=Crystal Engineering: A Textbook |last2=Vittal |first2=Jagadese J. |last3=Ramanan |first3=Arunachalam |date=2011 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4338-75-2 |language=en}}</ref> and weak hydrogen bonds.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last1=Desiraju |first1=Gautam |url=http://www.oxfordscholarship.com/view/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198509707.001.0001/acprof-9780198509707 |title=The Weak Hydrogen Bond |last2=Steiner |first2=Thomas |date=May 31, 2001 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-850970-7 |chapter=The weak hydrogen bond in supramolecular chemistry |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198509707.003.0004}}</ref> In March 2026 he was awarded the 14th Ewald Prize <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ewald Prize |url=https://www.iucr.org/iucr/ewald-prize |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=www.iucr.org}}</ref> of the [[International Union of Crystallography]], the organization's highest award, given every three years.

==Biography==
{{BLP sources section|date=March 2026}}
Gautam Desiraju was born in [[Chennai|Chennai, India]]. After schooling at Cathedral and John Connon Boys School in [[Bombay]], he obtained a B.Sc. from St. Xavier's College, Bombay in 1972. Under the guidance of David Y. Curtin and Iain C. Paul, he gained a PhD in 1976 from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. He worked between 1976 and 1978 at the research laboratories of [[Eastman Kodak Company]] in Rochester, N.Y., U.S.A. From 1978 to 1979, he was a research fellow at the Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore. In 1979, he joined the [[University of Hyderabad]] as a lecturer, was promoted to reader in 1984, and became a professor in 1990. After 30 years at the University of Hyderabad, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Science]] in Bangalore in 2009.

Desiraju has guided the PhD work of about 40 students and mentored about 100 postdoctoral associates. He has authored more than 475 research papers.

He is a member of the editorial advisory boards of [[ChemComm|Chemical Communications]] and the [[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]. He is the editor-in-chief of [[Polyhedron]]. He chaired the first [[Gordon Research Conference]]s on Crystal Engineering in 2010 and served as president of the [[International Union of Crystallography]] from 2011 to 2014. In August 2017, he organised the 24th Congress and General Assembly of the International Union of Crystallography in Hyderabad, India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iucr2017.org/|title=IUCR - 2017 &#124; International Union of Crystallography}}</ref>

Desiraju has received honorary doctorate degrees from [[Universidad Nacional de Córdoba]], Argentina, [[Rayalaseema University]], Kurnool, and [[Gulbarga University]], Kalaburagi. He has won international awards such as the [[Alexander von Humboldt]] Forschungspreis and the [[TWAS]] award in Chemistry. He was awarded the Acharya P. C. Ray Medal (2015) by the [[University of Calcutta]] for innovation in science and technology, the ISA Medal (2018) for Science by the [[University of Bologna]], and the Van der Waals Prize (2023) by ICNI, Strasbourg.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

==Scholarly contributions==

Desiraju's contributions to [[crystal engineering]] have focused on the concept of the [[supramolecular]] [[synthon]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Desiraju |first=Gautam R. |date=1995 |title=Supramolecular Synthons in Crystal Engineering—A New Organic Synthesis |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.199523111 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |language=en |volume=34 |issue=21 |pages=2311–2327 |doi=10.1002/anie.199523111 |issn=0570-0833|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Desiraju has authored several commentaries on science, the evolution of chemistry as a subject,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Desiraju |first=Gautam R. |date=2005 |title=Chemistry – The middle kingdom |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/24110202 |journal=Current Science |volume=88 |issue=3 |pages=374–380 |jstor=24110202 |issn=0011-3891}}</ref> its emergence, complexity and practices.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Desiraju |first=Gautam R. |date=April 2012 |title=Bold strategies for Indian science |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/484159a |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=484 |issue=7393 |pages=159–160 |doi=10.1038/484159a |pmid=22498608 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He has also written articles about the state of science education and research in India<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-02-19 |title=The Hindu : Opinion / Leader Page Articles : China shows the way in science education |url=http://www.hinduonnet.com/2007/02/19/stories/2007021902651000.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501133353/http://www.hinduonnet.com/2007/02/19/stories/2007021902651000.htm |archive-date=2007-05-01 |website=www.hinduonnet.com}}</ref> and the current status of chemistry research in the country,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arunan |first1=Elangannan |last2=Brakaspathy |first2=Ramasamy |last3=Desiraju |first3=Gautam R. |last4=Sivaram |first4=Swaminathan |date=January 2, 2013 |title=Chemistry in India: Unlocking the Potential |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/anie.201206960 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=114–117 |doi=10.1002/anie.201206960 |pmid=23203775 |issn=1433-7851|url-access=subscription }}</ref> identifying problems and suggesting solutions for issues that stem from, amongst other parameters, the dichotomy between traditional values and the aspiration of an ancient culture to advance scientifically like the west. Despite being educated in America, Desiraju has advocated therefore, inculcating a sense of "Indian-ness" and self-worth in Indian students and young scientists towards a better understanding of India's place in our contemporary world.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kqXhxDKrxsY |title=Prof. Gautam Desiraju's advice for young people: How to make India great again |date=14 January 2023 |language=en |access-date=2023-07-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wgcS9wlb3vk |title=Prof Desiraju Video Pondy Lit Fest 12 February 2023 on Bharat: India:2.0 |date=14 February 2023 |language=en |access-date=2023-07-12}}</ref>
